post.description:
Runs a query of the user analytics catalog (see `GET /api/analytics/_schema`) on the PostgreSQL database of the active user-analytics data exporter and returns its result.

This is how the user analytics dashboards get their data: read a dashboard with `GET /apis/analytics.otoroshi.io/v1/user-dashboards/{id}`, then run one query per widget with its `query` and `params`.

The result is always restricted to the tenant (organization) given by the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header, and is cached for 30 seconds unless `nocache` is `true`. Only the leaders of a cluster (or an instance out of any cluster) serve this endpoint.

Built-in queries (admin extensions can add more):

| id | shape | params | compare |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requests_total` | `scalar` | | yes |
| `errors_total` | `scalar` | | yes |
| `requests_by_status` | `pie` | | no |
| `requests_by_method` | `pie` | | no |
| `requests_by_route` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_by_api` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_by_apikey` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_by_user` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_by_domain` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_by_country` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `top_error_routes` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_per_second` | `timeseries` (`points`) | | yes |
| `error_rate_ts` | `timeseries` (`points`) | | yes |
| `duration_avg_ts` | `timeseries` (`points`) | | yes |
| `overhead_avg_ts` | `timeseries` (`points`) | | yes |
| `duration_percentiles_ts` | `timeseries` (`series`: `p50`, `p75`, `p95`, `p99`) | | yes |
| `traffic_in_out_ts` | `timeseries` (`series`: `data_in`, `data_out`) | | yes |
| `requests_by_status_class_ts` | `timeseries` (`series`: `2xx`, `3xx`, `4xx`, `5xx`) | | yes |
| `response_time_heatmap` | `heatmap` | | no |

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Tenant
parameters.description: The tenant (organization) whose data is read, `default` when absent. The admin must be a super admin or allowed to read it, and the answer is always restricted to it

requestBody.description: The query to run: the id of a query of the catalog, its parameters, the data it runs on, the size of its time buckets, and whether to compare it with the previous period or to skip the cache

200.description: The result of the query on the time range, with its result on the previous period when `compare` is asked for and the query supports it

400.description: The credentials are missing, the body is not valid json, or the query failed on the database

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is neither a super admin nor allowed to read the tenant (organization) of the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header

404.description: The query does not exist, or the instance is a worker of a cluster

412.description: No user-analytics data exporter is active

415.description: The body is not sent as `application/json`

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

500.description: The analytics runtime is not initialized yet: otoroshi sets it up one second after it starts

get.summary: Read the catalog of user analytics queries
get.description: Lists every query `POST /api/analytics/_query` can run, admin extensions included, with the shape of its result, the widget that displays it by default, its parameters and whether it supports period comparison. Also lists the widget types a dashboard widget can use.

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Tenant
parameters.description: The tenant (organization) the admin must be allowed to read, unless it is a super admin, `default` when absent. The answer does not depend on it

200.description: The catalog of the queries, the ones of the admin extensions included, and the widget types of the dashboards

400.description: The credentials are missing: the call carries no api key, and the route that serves the admin api refuses it before the controller runs

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is neither a super admin nor allowed to read the tenant (organization) of the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

500.description: The analytics runtime is not initialized yet: otoroshi sets it up one second after it starts

get.summary: List the event families user analytics can store
get.description: Lists the event families (projections) the user-analytics data exporter can store, admin extensions included, and the table each one is written to. Any of them can be left out with the `excluded_projections` setting of the exporter.

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: The PostgreSQL schema used to compute the `table` of each projection. The default of the exporter (`public`) when absent or blank

parameters.name: table_prefix
parameters.description: The table prefix used to compute the `table` of each projection. The default of the exporter (`otoroshi_analytics_events`) when absent or blank

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Tenant
parameters.description: The tenant (organization) the admin must be allowed to read, unless it is a super admin, `default` when absent. The answer does not depend on it

200.description: The event families the exporter can store, the core ones first, with the table each one is written to

post.summary: Test the connection to a user analytics database
post.description: Opens a single connection to the PostgreSQL database described by the body (the `config` of a user-analytics data exporter), runs `SELECT 1` on it and closes it. Super admins only.

requestBody.description: The settings of the database to test, the `config` of a user-analytics data exporter. Its `uri` is used when present, the other connection settings otherwise

400.description: The credentials are missing, the body is not valid json, or the connection failed (`ok` is `false` and `error` tells why)

schema.description: Why the connection failed, or why the call was refused

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is not a super admin

415.description: The body is not sent as `application/json`

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

post.summary: Make a user-analytics data exporter the active one
post.description: Makes the user-analytics data exporter `id` the one user analytics reads from (flagged by its `otoroshi:user-analytics:active` metadata), removes the flag from the other user-analytics data exporters, then creates the default dashboards that are missing. A disabled exporter is flagged but not read until it is enabled. Super admins only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of the user-analytics data exporter, a data exporter entity whose `type` is `user-analytics`

200.description: The exporter is now the active one: the number of exporters it replaces and the default dashboards it created

400.description: The credentials are missing: the call carries no api key, and the route that serves the admin api refuses it before the controller runs

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is not a super admin

404.description: No user-analytics data exporter has this id

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

post.description: Creates again the default user dashboards that are missing (the ones whose `otoroshi-default-id` metadata no dashboard holds anymore). Existing dashboards are never modified. Super admins only.

200.description: The default dashboards that were missing are created

400.description: The credentials are missing: the call carries no api key, and the route that serves the admin api refuses it before the controller runs

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is not a super admin

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

500.description: The default dashboards could not be created

get.summary: List the fired events of a user alert
get.description: Answers the times the user alert fired, newest first, with the evaluation of its conditions and their acknowledgement. The events are read from the database of the active user-analytics data exporter, in the tenant (organization) of the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header.

parameters.name: alertId
parameters.description: The id of the user alert, the `id` of an `analytics.otoroshi.io` user alert entity

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of events answered, brought back between 1 and 2000. 200 when absent or not an integer

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The number of events skipped, 0 when absent, negative or not an integer

parameters.name: seen
parameters.description: `true` only answers the acknowledged events, `false` the events not acknowledged yet. Every event when absent

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Tenant
parameters.description: The tenant (organization) whose data is read, `default` when absent. The admin must be a super admin or allowed to read it, and the answer is always restricted to it

200.description: A page of the fired events of the alert, newest first

400.description: The credentials are missing: the call carries no api key, and the route that serves the admin api refuses it before the controller runs

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is neither a super admin nor allowed to read the tenant (organization) of the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header

412.description: No user-analytics data exporter is active

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

500.description: The database of the active user-analytics data exporter could not be queried

post.summary: Acknowledge all the fired events of a user alert
post.description: Marks every event of the user alert not acknowledged yet as seen, now, by the admin behind the credentials (its email, `?` for an api key used without a backoffice user), and answers how many were. The events live in the database of the active user-analytics data exporter, in the tenant (organization) of the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header.
